400H: Evac+Chair Evacuation Stair Chair with 440 lb Capacity
Product URL: https://www.anchortex.com/products/evac-chair-power-400h-evacuation-stair-chair
Manufacturer page: https://evac-chair.com/evacchair-400h/
Spec sheets: 400H data sheet, Evac+Chair range brochure
Keywords (Ricky's sheet): Primary: power stair chair (100/mo). Secondary: powered stair climber (80, KD0), motorized evacuation chair (20), powered evacuation chair (0-10), evac chair power 400h (0). Ricky's note: powered version of the 300H; battery powered evacuation chair and electric stair evacuation chair are not indexed.
Recommended H1 and Subtitle
H1: Evac+Chair Evacuation Stair Chair with 440 lb Capacity, Armrests, and Footrest – 400H
Current H1: Evac+Chair Power 400H Evacuation Stair Chair
Subtitle: Manual Evacuation Chair with Self-Braking Wide-Tread Tracks, a Dual-Position Seat, and a 4-Point Harness for One-Person Evacuation Down the Stairs
Current subtitle: Evac+Chair 400H Evacuation Stair Chair
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair 400H is an evacuation stair chair based on the Evac+Chair 300H, with a higher weight capacity of 440 lbs and more support for the passenger. Evac+Chair developed it with occupational therapists, adding passenger armrests, a footrest, and a 4-point quick release harness, while keeping the chair light enough for one person to operate.
It is a manual chair for going down the stairs, with no motor or battery. Self-braking Evac+Track friction tracks, with a wider tread and adjustable tension, control the speed of descent to suit most staircases, so a small operator can move a passenger up to three times their size with no heavy lifting. The dual-position seat works as a flat seat or a hammock seat, and the chair folds to 8” deep for wall mounting near the stairwell.
Tracks: Evac+Track self-braking friction tracks with a wider tread and adjustable tension, to control the speed of descent on most staircases
Seat: Dual-position seat: a flat seat with zipped side panels and an over-thigh quick release restraint, or a hammock seat (release the side panels and fasten them underneath)
Harness: 4-point quick release safety harness
Head Restraint: Adjustable head restraint limits movement and secures the passenger
Armrests and Footrest: Passenger armrests for comfort and safety; footrest for a stable seating position on the stairs
Handle: Ergonomic adjustable handle for easy deployment and compact storage
Wheels: Heavy duty wheels for uneven ground; lockable rear wheels keep the chair still when needed
Operation: One operator; down the stairs only
Stairs: Straight staircases (not spiral), at least 23” wide, with a 20° to 40° angle
Weight Capacity: 440 lbs
Weight: 30 lbs
Folded Size: 20”W×8”D×41”H
Certifications: FDA registered
Includes: 4-point quick release harness, photoluminescent signage, wall mounting brackets, dust cover, and user guide
Warranty: Lifetime manufacturer’s warranty
Available Models and Options
400H – Evacuation Stair Chair: Dual-position seat, armrests and footrest, one-person operation, 440 lb capacity, 30 lbs
[H2] Applications
The 400H suits buildings with stairs where heavier passengers, or people who need more support, may need help getting out in an emergency.
Typical applications include:
Offices, hotels, and high-rise buildings
Hospitals, senior living, and care facilities
Schools, universities, and public buildings
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
Is the Evac+Chair 400H a power stair chair?
No. The 400H has no motor or battery. It is a manual evacuation chair that uses self-braking tracks to control the speed of descent. For a powered stair climber, Evac+Chair makes the battery powered Power 800 and Power 900.
How is the 400H different from the 300H?
The 400H is based on the 300H but has a higher weight capacity (440 lbs instead of 400 lbs), passenger armrests and a footrest, a 4-point harness, and wider tracks with adjustable tension. The 300H is lighter, at 19 lbs.
How many people does it take to operate the 400H?
One. The 400H is designed for single person operation, and the self-braking tracks let a small operator move a passenger up to three times their size.
Can the 400H go up the stairs?
No. It is for downward evacuation on straight staircases. For upward evacuation, Evac+Chair makes the 600H, which has carry handles, and the Power 800 and Power 900 stair climbing chairs.
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
NOT POWERED: our page calls this chair the "Power 400H," but it has no motor or battery. Evac+Chair calls it the "Evac+Chair 400H," and its web page, data sheet, and brochure (and our own current description) describe a manual chair with self-braking friction tracks for going down the stairs. I took "Power" out of the recommended H1 and meta title. The URL (…power-400h…) is not changed.
Keywords: Ricky's keywords for this page are all for powered chairs ("power stair chair," "powered stair climber," "motorized evacuation chair," "powered evacuation chair"), so they do not fit this product. I used "power stair chair" and "powered stair climber" only in an honest FAQ ("Is the 400H a power stair chair? No."), as we did with "evacuation wheelchair" on the 600H. The H1 and meta title use the product's own name, "evacuation stair chair," which is also the 300H page's primary keyword. Ricky, could you suggest another primary keyword for this page?
Weight: the 400H data sheet (VERS 2/400/7-24) says 30 lbs; the Evac+Chair web page, range brochure, and our current page say 33 lbs. I used the data sheet, as you said for the 700H folded size.
Harness: the data sheet and web page say 4-point; the range brochure says 5-point. I used 4-point (data sheet).
Stairs: from the data sheet: straight staircases only (no spiral), down only, at least 23” wide, 20° to 40° angle.
Price: $2,150 with no compare-at price. The other Evac+Chair pages have a compare-at price (price = 75%); the 600H is also $2,150, with compare-at $2,867. Should the 400H have a compare-at price?
Left out: "not available in other alternatives," "superior quality," "World's No.1," "beware of poor imitations," 9/11, and "exceeds fire safety requirements ... Americans with Disabilities Act."
Duplicate content: our current description is the Evac+Chair web page text word for word, plus an old "About Evac+Chair of North America" paragraph. The new copy is fully rewritten.
Images: the 3 current images are kept (numbered features diagram 941×934, and side views of the flat and hammock seats 600×710). Evac+Chair has a photo of the 400H in use on a stairwell (1920×1080). Would you like me to add it as "Evac-Chair-400H-Evacuation-Stair-Chair-Stairwell-View.jpg"?
Shipping weight: the variant is set to 200 lbs; the chair weighs 30 lbs. Is 200 lbs a placeholder, as on the other Evac+Chair pages?
Current meta description is the general GSA pricing line. GSA is not mentioned in the description, per your note on the other tabs.
